title: Wayward House Mathematics
text:
0.1 What this is testing
This mock is meant to answer one question: what happens if we stop wrapping the book in the website chrome and instead style Quarto’s own book structure directly?

title: Wayward House Mathematics
text:
the native Quarto sidebar as the real book navigation

title: Wayward House Mathematics
text:
0.2 What this intentionally avoids

moving DOM nodes after render
rewriting links in JavaScript
layering a second site shell on top of the book shell
book-specific CSS fighting site-wide header and footer overrides

title: Wayward House Mathematics
text:
0.3 The hypothesis
If this feels structurally cleaner, the next step is not “more overrides.” It is migrating the maths book to a dedicated format extension and letting the extension own the book presentation from the start.

title: 2  Sample Chapter
text:
2.1 Why a bespoke format might be cleaner
The current maths book inherits the Quarto book shell, then replaces parts of it with Wayward website chrome, then patches the remaining seams with CSS and JavaScript. That makes every layout decision harder than it needs to be.

title: 2  Sample Chapter
text:
2.1.1 Where the collisions happen

book sidebar versus injected site header
native Quarto content grid versus custom full-width reading layouts
native repo tools versus rewritten links
page footer expectations versus after-body injection



2.1.2 What a dedicated format would own

Typography and spacing
Sidebar look and collapse behavior
TOC placement and width
Footer content and presentation
Theme tokens and book-only utilities







Note



This page is deliberately plain in content so we can judge the shell rather than the prose.

title: 2  Sample Chapter
text:
2.2 A simple section for testing
The native Quarto book structure is already doing most of the right things. The main question is whether we can make it feel like Wayward House without trying to turn it into the main site itself.

2.2.1 Another section
This mock should give us a cleaner basis for deciding whether to build a full custom template, or whether a custom format plus native Quarto book components is already enough.
